meta.description: Batch program that sequentially reads and prints all customer records from the customer master file for reporting or audit purposes.
meta.process_description: This program opens the customer master file and reads every customer record sequentially from start to finish, displaying each record to the system output. It is the customer data equivalent of CBACT02C (which does the same for card records), serving as a full customer data extract or audit report. The program handles end-of-file gracefully and will abnormally terminate (ABEND) with a diagnostic code if any unexpected file I/O error occurs, ensuring data integrity issues are surfaced immediately.

files.CUSTFILE: Customer master file (VSAM KSDS) containing all customer demographic and profile records, keyed by customer ID

business_rules: Every customer record in the master file must be read and printed — no filtering or selection criteria are applied, ensuring a complete audit trail.
The customer file must be accessible and openable; failure to open the file results in an immediate abnormal program termination (ABEND), preventing partial or misleading output.
Any unexpected I/O error during record reading (other than normal end-of-file) causes an immediate ABEND with diagnostic status codes, ensuring data integrity issues are not silently ignored.
Records are processed in customer ID sequence (sequential access on a KSDS VSAM file), providing an ordered, reproducible output suitable for reconciliation or audit.
Normal end-of-file is the only acceptable termination condition for the read loop; all other conditions are treated as errors.

variables.name: FD-CUSTFILE-REC
variables.description: The physical record layout for a single customer as it is read directly from the Customer Master File (CUSTFILE). This is the raw buffer that receives each customer record from disk before its contents are interpreted for reporting.

variables.name: FD-CUST-ID
variables.description: The unique 9-digit customer identifier as stored in the physical file record. This is the primary key that uniquely identifies each customer in the Customer Master File and determines the sequential order in which records are read and reported.

variables.name: FD-CUST-DATA
variables.description: The remaining 491 bytes of the customer's raw profile data as read from the Customer Master File. This payload contains all personal and account-related customer information (name, address, SSN, credit score, etc.) that will be mapped into the structured CUSTOMER-RECORD layout for display and reporting.

variables.name: CUSTFILE-STATUS
variables.description: The two-character VSAM file status code returned by the operating system after every open, read, or close operation on the Customer Master File. The program inspects this code to determine whether each file operation succeeded, reached end-of-file, or encountered an error requiring an abnormal termination.

variables.name: CUSTFILE-STAT1
variables.description: The first character of the Customer Master File status code, representing the major status category (e.g., '0' for successful operation, '1' for end-of-file, '9' for a hardware or VSAM-level error). Used to quickly classify whether the last file operation was successful or problematic.

variables.name: CUSTFILE-STAT2
variables.description: The second character of the Customer Master File status code, providing a more specific sub-code that further describes the nature of a file operation result. Together with CUSTFILE-STAT1, it gives the full diagnostic code used to identify the exact cause of any file I/O failure.

variables.name: IO-STATUS
variables.description: A general-purpose two-character I/O status holder used to capture and carry file operation status codes for error diagnosis and reporting. It serves as a working area to consolidate status information when converting or displaying error codes during abnormal termination handling.

variables.name: IO-STAT1
variables.description: The first character of the general I/O status code, representing the major category of the file operation result. Used during error reporting to communicate the primary nature of a file failure to operators or downstream diagnostic processes.

variables.name: IO-STAT2
variables.description: The second character of the general I/O status code, providing the specific sub-code detail of a file operation result. Together with IO-STAT1, it forms the complete diagnostic status used to pinpoint the exact nature of a file error during abnormal termination.

variables.name: TWO-BYTES-BINARY
variables.description: A 2-byte binary numeric work area used as an intermediate conversion field. It allows the program to interpret a numeric status or result code in binary form so that its individual byte components can be extracted and examined separately for error diagnosis.

variables.name: TWO-BYTES-ALPHA
variables.description: An alphanumeric overlay of the TWO-BYTES-BINARY field that allows the same 2-byte memory area to be read as two individual characters. This enables the program to split a binary status code into its left and right byte components for character-level inspection and error reporting.

variables.name: TWO-BYTES-LEFT
variables.description: The left (high-order) byte of the binary status code when viewed as two separate characters. Used to extract the major category portion of a converted status code for inclusion in error messages or diagnostic output during abnormal termination.

variables.name: TWO-BYTES-RIGHT
variables.description: The right (low-order) byte of the binary status code when viewed as two separate characters. Used to extract the specific sub-code portion of a converted status code for inclusion in error messages or diagnostic output during abnormal termination.

variables.name: IO-STATUS-04
variables.description: A structured work area used to decompose and display a numeric I/O status code in a human-readable format for error reporting. It breaks the status into a 1-digit major code and a 3-digit minor code, making it easier for operators to diagnose file access failures.

variables.name: IO-STATUS-0401
variables.description: The single-digit major category of the I/O status code, initialized to zero (success). During error handling, this field holds the primary status digit that classifies the type of file operation failure encountered when reading the Customer Master File.

variables.name: IO-STATUS-0403
variables.description: The three-digit minor detail code of the I/O status, initialized to zero (no error). During error handling, this field holds the specific sub-code that further describes the exact nature of a file operation failure, providing detailed diagnostic information for operators investigating a Customer Master File access problem.

variables.name: APPL-RESULT
variables.description: The internal application result code that tracks the outcome of each customer file read operation. The program sets this code after each read attempt and uses it to decide whether to continue processing records, stop at end-of-file, or trigger an abnormal termination due to an unexpected error.

variables.name: APPL-AOK
variables.description: A condition name that evaluates to true when the last customer file read operation completed successfully (result code = 0). When this condition is true, the program proceeds to print the customer record and reads the next one, continuing the normal batch reporting cycle.

variables.name: APPL-EOF
variables.description: A condition name that evaluates to true when the Customer Master File has been fully read and no more customer records remain (result code = 16, end-of-file). This is the only acceptable way for the read loop to terminate, signalling that all customers have been successfully reported.

variables.name: END-OF-FILE
variables.description: A processing control flag that tracks whether all customer records in the Customer Master File have been read. Initialized to 'N' (not finished), it is set to 'Y' when end-of-file is reached, signalling the batch loop to stop reading and proceed to close the file and end the report.

variables.name: ABCODE
variables.description: The abnormal termination (ABEND) code passed to the system abend handler when a fatal error occurs, such as failure to open the Customer Master File or an unexpected I/O error during reading. A value of 999 is used to signal a critical batch failure, ensuring the error is visible in job logs and prevents silent data integrity issues.

variables.name: TIMING
variables.description: A binary numeric field used to pass a timing or delay parameter to the system abend handler at the point of abnormal termination. It controls the behaviour of the abend call, such as whether a system dump should be produced immediately or after a short interval, aiding in post-failure diagnostics.

paragraphs.name: 1000-CUSTFILE-GET-NEXT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph retrieves the next customer record from the master file and displays it for audit or reporting purposes. It distinguishes between a successful read, a normal end-of-file condition, and any unexpected I/O error — aborting the program immediately if data integrity cannot be guaranteed.

paragraphs.name: 0000-CUSTFILE-OPEN
paragraphs.description: This paragraph attempts to open the customer master file in preparation for a full sequential read of all customer records. If the file cannot be opened, the program immediately halts with a fatal error, preventing any partial or misleading audit output from being produced.

paragraphs.name: 9000-CUSTFILE-CLOSE
paragraphs.description: This paragraph safely closes the customer master file after all records have been read and reported. It verifies the file closed successfully and triggers an immediate abnormal termination with diagnostic output if the closure fails, protecting data integrity.

paragraphs.name: Z-ABEND-PROGRAM
paragraphs.description: This paragraph handles unrecoverable processing failures by immediately halting the program with a formal abnormal termination signal. It ensures that any critical error — such as a file I/O failure on the customer master file — is surfaced visibly to operations staff rather than silently producing incomplete or misleading audit output.

paragraphs.name: Z-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS
paragraphs.description: This paragraph formats and displays a human-readable diagnostic message whenever a file input/output error occurs during customer record processing. It ensures that operators and auditors receive a clear, standardized error code to identify and investigate any failure accessing the customer master file.
